title: Head-in-Head in Linear Attention
claim: A standard block is extended with a structured state-transition matrix built from several projected inputs, which updates memory and produces the output.
layout: 2 panels, bottom-to-top flow, left block zoomed into right detail, legend on top
description: The figure has two gray rounded panels. The left panel shows a transformer-style layer drawn bottom to top: RMSNorm, then an HH-GDN block, then a residual addition, then RMSNorm, SwiGLU and another residual addition. A dashed arrow from HH-GDN opens the right panel, which shows the block's internals. A legend at the top defines the symbols for matrix multiplication, elementwise multiplication, outer product and elementwise addition. The input x_t goes to five blue Linear layers. These produce M_org, alpha_t, beta_t, k_t, v_t and q_t. Short-Convolution and green L2Norm modules sit on the k, v and q paths. The pink State Transition Matrix A_t box is built from M_org, alpha and beta. The previous state S_{t-1} is multiplied by A_t, added to the k-v outer product, and produces S_t. S_t is multiplied by q_t to give o_t. Colors mark module types: peach for blocks, yellow for norms, blue for linear layers, green for L2Norm and pink for the state transition matrix.
caption: Model Architecture of Head-in-Head Linear Attention, using Head-in-Head Gated-DeltaNet (HH-GDN) for example. We use
abstract: The state-transition (decay) matrix governs how fixed-size memory is updated and used, making it a core design in linear attention models. Prior work exploits rank-1 approximations to reduce the cost of constructing decay matrices, but this low-rank constraint also limits the expressive capacity. We therefore formulate decay-matrix design as an open optimization problem: maximizing expressiveness while introducing minimal additional cost. Inspired by the multi-head mechanism, we propose Head-in-Head, which introduces an additional mask matrix to structure memory partitioning and interactions within a single linear-attention head. This simple, generic, and efficient design: 1) enables a rank-$r$ approximation of the decay matrix with only a few extra parameters and 2) strengthens intra-head information interaction. We further develop mask normalization and a chunk-wise parallelization scheme to support efficient parallel training. Extensive experiments on synthetic benchmarks and language modeling tasks, together with visual analyses, show that Head-in-Head consistently improves baseline performance by enriching information diversity and strengthening intra-head interactions. Code available at: \url{https://github.com/msj-19/Head-in-Head-Linear-Attention}
